Chapter I

What to Bring Back

For yourself, friends & family

🌶️

Epices Roellinger

The finest spice shop in Paris

Le Marais, 75003

One of the best spice shops in Paris. Incredible quality, unique blends you can't find anywhere else. The aromas alone are worth the visit.

Must-buys

  • Poudre des Fees
  • Poudre a braises
  • Poudre 4 epices a la francaise
  • Ras el hanout (Moroccan spices)
♦
🍵

Mariage Freres

Iconic French tea house since 1854

15-min walk from the office

Iconic French tea house since 1854. Buy in canisters — they make great gifts too. The store itself is a beautiful experience.

My picks

  • Marco Polo
  • Earl Grey French Blue
  • Casablanca
♦
🍷

Wine

Neighborhood wine stores

Go to any local wine shop — or Nicolas (a reliable chain with locations everywhere). Grab 4 bottles, all under $20 each. French wine at this price point is unbeatable.

Recommendations

  • Tariquet Dernieres Grives — sweet white wine, amazing
  • Roussette de Savoie — dry white, perfect with cheese
  • Pic Saint-Loup — light red wine
  • Crozes-Hermitage — Syrah, fuller red
Pro Tip

Buy bubble wine bags on Amazon before you leave → Get them here — I bring back 8 bottles every trip, never had an issue!

♦
🏠

Pierre Guillaume

Home fragrance

15-min walk — 13 Rue Jean-Jacques Rousseau, 75001 Paris

Love their home parfums — unique scents you won't find in the US. A special souvenir for your home. Their fragrances are artisanal and beautifully crafted.

♦
👔

Balibaris

French menswear

Great French brand for men. Clean, stylish, well-priced. Think smart casual with a French touch. Perfect for upgrading your wardrobe with pieces that have that effortless Parisian style.

♦
🛒

Grocery Store Haul

Monoprix (recommended) or Carrefour

Head to a Monoprix — they're everywhere in Paris and have a great selection of French food products. Carrefour works too. Grab these essentials:

Grab these

  • Nestle Dessert Chocolat Noir (baking chocolate, absolute game changer)
  • Pâté (meat spread — great for appetizers and snacking)
  • Honey & jams
  • Fleur de sel de Guerande (sea salt — elevates everything you cook)
  • French mustard — look for Maille brand, way better than what we get in the US
  • Bonne Maman anything (cheaper in France!)
  • Savon de Marseille — classic multi-purpose French soap, beautiful and inexpensive
Pro Tip

Short on time? Head to La Grande Épicerie de Paris or Lafayette Gourmet (Galeries Lafayette food hall) — they have most of these items under one roof, curated and ready to go.

♦
🧀

Cheese

Yes, you can bring it back!

You are allowed to bring cheese back to the US. Technically only pasteurized, but I've never had any issue with it. Go to a fromagerie (cheese store) and have them vacuum seal it — it travels perfectly.

Pro Tip

Everything below can be frozen once you're back home until you need it. I bring these back every single trip.

What I bring back

  • Raclette cheese — for raclette nights at home, nothing beats the real thing
  • Fondue Savoyarde — it's a mix of 3 different cheeses. Ask the fromagerie to give you the right combination for fondue Savoyarde, they'll know exactly what to prepare
♦
💊

French Pharmacy

Don't skip this!

French pharmacies (look for the green cross ✚ sign) sell skincare that's 2-3x cheaper than in the US. Stock up for yourself and as gifts.

Must-buys

  • La Roche-Posay (sunscreen, moisturizers)
  • Bioderma (micellar water)
  • Avene (thermal water spray, moisturizers)
  • Embryolisse (the cult French moisturizer)
  • Homeoplasmine (the French multi-purpose balm everyone swears by)
♦
Chapter II

What to Do

If you have a few hours free

Short on time? Here are two walks I'd recommend — both are doable in a couple of hours.

Montmartre & Sacré-Cœur

This is where I live!

Exit at Metro Abbesses. Walk to Place Saint-Pierre, then go up the hill to Sacré-Cœur for the best view of Paris. Then walk behind the basilica to Place du Tertre — artists, cafés, and the village feel of old Paris. Perfect for a morning or late afternoon stroll.

Saint-Michel → Notre-Dame

Ice cream + cathedral

Exit at Metro Saint-Michel. Stop at my favorite ice cream place in Europe, then walk north along the Seine to Notre-Dame de Paris. A beautiful walk, especially in the evening.

Chapter III

Where to Eat

Skip the tourist traps

My advice: go to neighborhood restaurants. Avoid the big tourist spots — the food is better and cheaper in local places. Here are my recommendations:

🍦

Gelateria La Romana

Near Saint-Michel — the best ice cream I've ever had. Worth the detour every single time.

Google Maps
🥐

Cedric Grolet Opera

5-min walk from the office. World-famous pastry chef — incredible trompe-l'oeil fruit pastries. Go to the Café in the back for a shorter line.

Website
🍷

Neighborhood Brasserie

The real Parisian experience. Pick any small brasserie with a short menu and locals eating there — that's usually a good sign. Order the plat du jour (daily special), a glass of wine, and enjoy. This is how Parisians eat every day.

Restaurant Recommendations

🌿

📍 18 Rue du Château d’Eau, 75010

📍 4 Rue Stanislas, 75006

📍 7 Rue Stanislas, 75006

East Mamma

Basque restaurant — pintxos, chipirons, gâteau basque. A taste of the French southwest in Paris.

📍 20 Rue du Général Guilhem, 75011

Natural wine bar & bistro in Montmartre. Cozy spot with seasonal small plates and excellent natural wines.

📍 104 Rue Caulaincourt, 75018

Brasserie Dubillot

Modern French brasserie from the “Nouvelle Garde” group. Generous homemade brasserie cuisine.

📍 222 Rue Saint-Denis, 75002

Classic Parisian bouillon — affordable, traditional French comfort food. Great for a hearty, budget-friendly meal.

💰

Detaxe (Tax Refund)

Don't leave money on the table!

Every time you spend more than ~100 EUR in a single store, you can get a VAT refund (~12% back)!

How it works

  1. 1Ask the store to fill out the detaxe form (show them your passport — photo on your phone works)
  2. 2At departure, look for the Detaxe / Tax Refund location. Scan your receipts at a kiosk — no need to see an agent, it's pretty quick.
  3. 3Green screen = validated ✅ — refund hits your card in a few weeks
Flying from Paris CDG or Orly

Look for the Detaxe kiosks at the airport. Do it BEFORE checking your luggage / before the security.

Taking the Eurostar to London

Detaxe kiosks are at Gare du Nord! Go through the ticket gates, customs & security, then follow the "Detaxe" signs. Since the UK is no longer in the EU (post-Brexit), Gare du Nord is your last EU exit point — you CANNOT do it in London.

Most stores in Paris handle detaxe routinely — just ask!

Before You Leave the US

Prep section

A few small purchases that make a big difference:

🍷

Bubble Wine Bags

Protect your bottles in checked luggage

Amazon
⚖️

Luggage Scale

Under $10 — maximize your luggage weight worry-free

Amazon
🔌

Electric Outlet Adapter

France uses Type C/E plugs (round pins). US plugs won't fit — grab a universal adapter or a US-to-EU adapter before you go. Available at any airport shop or Amazon.

💤

Melatonin

Buy some melatonin before leaving the US — it really helps with the jetlag. It's available over the counter in the US but much harder to find in France (it's regulated differently there). Take it the first few nights to reset your sleep schedule.
